page: Amazon Web Services m6g.8xlarge is a general-purpose instance powered by AWS Graviton processors. It features 32 dedicated physical cores based on the ARMv8 64-bit architecture, specifically utilizing the AWS Neoverse-N1 CPU model running at 2.5 GHz. Because the processor operates with 1.0 thread per core, each of the 32 vCPUs corresponds to a dedicated physical core, eliminating resource contention associated with simultaneous multithreading. The instance is equipped with 128.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced allocation of 4.0 GB of RAM per core.

Built on the AWS Nitro System hypervisor, the m6g.8xlarge instance does not include local NVMe storage, relying instead on network-attached storage options. It provides a baseline network bandwidth of 12 Gbps. The Neoverse-N1 processor includes 64 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache per core, and a shared 32 MB L3 cache. Hardware-accelerated cryptography is supported via AES instructions, though x86-specific instruction sets such as AVX or AMX are absent due to the ARM64 architecture.

The ARM-based Graviton architecture is designed to deliver high resource density and power efficiency, offering a cost-effective alternative to comparable x86-based general-purpose instances for compatible software ecosystems. Lacking a dedicated GPU or local storage, this instance is optimized for workloads that benefit from balanced compute and memory footprints. Suitable applications include multi-threaded web serving, application servers, microservices, containerized deployments, caching fleets, and mid-sized database servers.
